title: Lesson 8 - Reports and dashboards in production: joined reports, dynamic dashboards, subscriptions, and row-level security
description: Identify ways to transform business outcomes and sales KPIs into reports and dashboards.

questions.question: Numbers on a dashboard differ depending on who opens it, and the team wants everyone to see the same company pipeline. What do you set?
options: Run as another user (a specific user)
questions.explanation: Running as one specific user renders one shared data scope for all viewers, which is the stated goal.

questions.question: A monthly KPI email arrives with an empty report because the schedule runs as a user whose role hides the records. What is the fix?
options: Convert the report to a joined report
Set the scheduled report to run as a user with access to all the required records
questions.explanation: A scheduled report runs as the specified user, so that user must be able to see every record the report should include.

questions.question: A stakeholder wants to chart how pipeline coverage changed over a year, but the live report shows only current values. Which feature do you use?
questions.explanation: A reporting snapshot writes report results into a custom object over time, which is what lets you chart change the live report cannot show.
